newsitem.title: UK: FIMAT Metals to seek greater LME market share.
newsitem.headline: FIMAT Metals to seek greater LME market share.

text.p: FIMAT Metals Ltd, established on Monday, is looking to increase its share of metals business by utilising its capacity to offer a much wider range of products, Francois Defferriere, managing director of FIMAT UK said.

"Societe Generale can offer a full range of products (to customers) in the base metals, covering London Metal Exchange (LME), OTC (over-the-counter), corporate and structured financing and stock financing," he said in an interview.

FIMAT Metals futures and options broking in listed contracts on the LME will be complementary to Societe Generale's OTC base metals derivatives group based in Paris and will allow the Societe Generale Group to offer a comprehensive service in base metals, Fimat said.
FIMAT Metals comprises the metals team of LME ring-dealer Brody White, a U.S. commodity broker FIMAT acquired this year.
The 10 existing staff will be augmented by five new appointments, who will be arriving over the coming weeks, Mark Slade, director of FIMAT Metals LME division said.

"Brody White was one of the smaller LME companies, but FIMAT is looking to become of the leading companies on the Exchange...We are stronger than some of the other banks (in metals), because they are not ring-dealers," Slade said.
FIMAT UK is virtually wholly-owned by FIMAT International Banque, which is a 100-percent subsidiary of France's Societe Generale Group.
Defferriere said that Societe Generale has had expertise in OTC products for some years via it's base metals derivatives team which is based in Paris.
So this is not a new venture for the company but it will sit alongside the existing LME operations of the former Brody White which are now fully incorporated.
"By combining the two the Societe Generale Group can offer a full spectrum of what our customers want...The customer wants people to offer innovative products," he said.
FIMAT International has some 1,100 people in around 15 countries at present, and will utilise these resources to increase its customer coverage, Defferriere said.

It has set up an LME desk in Tokyo and also has New York metals operatives. But its priority at the moment is to develop capacity on the LME and it has done this by bringing in personnel who have more exposure to that market.
Although overall turnover in non-ferrous metals business has fallen since the Sumitomo Corp copper scandal in June, FIMAT was optimistic on the market outlook.
"We are working up from a small base and winning market share, and we can adjust to any changes in the market because we are not that large," Slade said.
FIMAT believes that metals will be an important growth area in the commodities sector in the next five to 10 years.
It already has a strong position in financial products and soft commodities, where it is one of the major players in the LIFFE cocoa, coffee and sugar markets, Defferriere said.
